chapter: Road shows in the Southwest and Midwest
title: Bill Bailey's Troubadours and the Musical Meat Market act
summary: The brothers join Bill Bailey's Troubadours and perform an instrumental act built around a butcher-shop set of props.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, that's what Nat Reece had, and he was a big one in those days, and so Hattie and them came over to us, and we did that two or three years, and we went East, and we worked in Kansas City for a Negro theater for awhile, and then we joined Bill Bailey's Troubadours, and we travelled with that for three or four months, and they got in bad...I mean, bad shape: The manager run off with all the money and stranded us, and I came home to Los Angeles but my brother

stayed and went back to Kansas City, I think, to work awhile, and then
... During those days that we were with Bill Bailey, we were doing
a musical instrumental act called "The Spikes Brothers' Meat Market."
It was to represent a meat market, and we played the counter stools
which was a xylophone and the sides of bacon which was saxophones put
inside the bacons and the saws was the violin bows and stools was
rattles. You know, you twist the stools around, and it rattled all
different keys, and the chopping block was an xylophone, too, and
the cash register was bells, and we dressed as butchers.
You had a lot of props to carry then, didn't you?

Yeah, we had four or five trunks of that stuff.
And anyway, I came home, and my brother and I--he went on his way and
I went on my way. Then he called me back to Denver, and from Denver
we worked awhile in a show called...I can't think of it now.
